sections.title: The decision and management’s recommendation
sections.body: Start with the specific choice, the recommendation, the alternatives, and the consequence of waiting. Distinguish a request for input from an item that needs a formal decision; confirm the approval process separately with the people responsible for governance.
sections.evidence: Decision brief, alternatives, decision deadline, and the person responsible for bringing the recommendation.
sections.question: What changes if we choose the alternative or defer the decision?

sections.title: What changed since the previous meeting
sections.body: Use the same reporting periods and definitions to compare actual results with the plan and the previous update. Lead with the material change. Separate what the team can explain from what it is still investigating, and connect the change to the recommendation.
sections.evidence: Actual-versus-plan bridge, prior meeting commitments, explanation of material variances, and unresolved causes with an investigation owner.
sections.question: Which change affects the plan, rather than only the explanation of last month?

sections.title: Cash, commitments, and the assumption that could move them
sections.body: Connect the cash position to dated receipts, committed payments, and choices still open. Show how the proposed decision changes those commitments. Identify the customer, hiring, or financing assumption that would cause management to revisit its recommendation.
sections.evidence: Reconciled cash position with any restrictions identified, dated receipt and payment assumptions, and an explicit alternative timing case.
sections.question: Which commitment would we revisit first if the key receipt or financing date moved?

sections.title: The bridge between the story and the numbers
sections.body: State the definition, reporting date, and source for each metric used in the decision. Distinguish contracted recurring revenue, live recurring revenue, recognized revenue, and cash receipts where relevant; do not require different measures to equal one another. Explain their timing and scope differences. If a prior number changes, show the correction and its cause rather than silently replacing the comparison.
sections.evidence: Metric definitions, source schedules, reporting cutoffs, and an explained bridge for material differences or corrections.
sections.question: Can another reader trace the headline number to its source and understand the difference from the financial statements?

sections.title: Operating owners and dependencies
sections.body: Ask each relevant leader to own the interpretation of their result, the proposed response, and the decision or help they need. Finance connects those inputs to the plan and checks consistency. Identify dependencies across teams instead of using the deck as a sequence of disconnected department updates.
sections.evidence: Named owners for the affected operating inputs, cross-team dependencies, and the action each leader proposes.
sections.question: Who owns the response, and what must another team deliver for it to work?

sections.title: Decisions, follow-ups, and supporting evidence
sections.body: Close the discussion with the outcome, accountable owner, next check-in, and condition that would reopen the decision. Keep detailed schedules available behind the main narrative. Agree the pre-read timing with the board and label the reporting cutoff so readers know what the package includes.
sections.evidence: Decision and action log, unresolved questions with owners and review dates, and clearly labeled supporting schedules.
sections.question: What will we check at the next review to know whether the chosen response is working?

focuses.label: Operating plan & priorities
focuses.title: The trade-off in the operating plan
focuses.body: Show which priority receives resources, what is deferred, and how the recommendation changes the plan. Connect functional milestones to the cash and capacity assumptions they depend on.
focuses.evidence: Current plan, proposed changes, dated commitments, and milestone owners.
focuses.question: Which assumption would make us change the resource allocation?

focuses.label: Cash & a spending commitment
focuses.title: The commitment and its cash dependency
focuses.body: Put the proposed commitment alongside dated receipts and obligations. Compare an explicit timing alternative, and show which choices remain reversible before committing spend.
focuses.evidence: Dated cash view, payment or collection assumptions, committed versus discretionary spend, and the commitment deadline.
focuses.question: What happens to this commitment if the receipt arrives later than planned?

focuses.label: Revenue & customer dependence
focuses.title: The customer change behind the revenue result
focuses.body: Explain which customer starts, expansions, losses, or implementation delays drive the change. Separate live from contracted recurring revenue when relevant. Connect a material customer dependency to the operating and cash response.
focuses.evidence: Customer-level movement schedule, metric definitions, implementation or renewal dates, and the resulting plan changes.
focuses.question: Which customer assumption supports the recommendation, and what changes if it does not hold?

focuses.label: Financing & the capital plan
focuses.title: The capital decision behind the operating plan
focuses.body: Show what the financing would fund, the milestones it supports, and the operating choices if timing changes. Separate confirmed commitments from intended financing. Use the diligence guide for the evidence behind an investor process.
focuses.evidence: Use-of-proceeds plan, financing status and timing assumptions, obligations, milestone owners, and an alternative operating path.
focuses.question: Which operating choice changes if the expected capital is delayed?

focuses.label: A material miss or emerging issue
focuses.title: The issue, what is known, and the response
focuses.body: State the miss and its consequence early. Separate verified causes from hypotheses. Show the proposed response, its owner, and the decision or assistance needed; make the unresolved evidence visible.
focuses.evidence: Extent of the variance, known versus unresolved causes, proposed response, and investigation owners and dates.
focuses.question: What evidence would change our explanation or our response?
